tools.description:
Create a draft tool (a script over your operations).

SCRIPT GUIDE. A tool is ONE deterministic async Python script run in an isolated sandbox. Send
files=[{"path":"tool.py","content":"..."}]; the entrypoint is tool:main, i.e.
`async def main(inputs, ctx)` returning the result envelope. The host adds kit.py (helpers) and
ops.py (operation table): never send them, just `import kit`. Standard library only; the only way
out of the sandbox is kit.call.
Calling your operations: the script key is "<source_key>.<op_key>" (platform service operations:
"<service>.<op_key>"), exactly the entries of `ops`. Arguments are the operation's input_schema
fields (see builder_operation_list).
  status, body = await kit.call(ctx, "crm.get_customer", {"id": inputs["id"]})
    -> (200, body); or (status, body) for a 4xx the operation lists in expected_error_statuses.
       Any other failure raises RuntimeError("api_call_denied").
  body = await kit.call_ok(ctx, key, args, what="load customer")   # non-200 ends the tool with backend_error
  return await kit.guarded(run(inputs, ctx))                        # turns aborts/denied calls into envelopes
Result envelope (build it with the helpers; invariants are enforced):
  kit.completed(data, checks, next_steps)        -> status ok (check_failed if a check fails)
  kit.check(name, "pass"|"fail"|"degraded"|"error", summary)   # name: lowercase snake_case
  kit.precondition_failed(reason, [kit.step("other_tool", "why")])   # reason: snake_case
  kit.backend_error("message", retryable=False)
  kit.pending(token, next_steps) with kit.encode_token(tool, state) / kit.decode_token(token, tool)
  kit.step(tool, reason, arguments); kit.clip(text); kit.Budget(wall_seconds) and kit.poll(...)
    for bounded waiting; kit.describe(status, body) summarises an unexpected HTTP status.
Write tools: set effect="writes" if ANY operation the tool uses writes; test them with
confirm_writes=true only against data you accept changing.

public_name.description: the MCP tool name callers will see, e.g. crm_find_customer

tools.name: builder_tool_create

tools.description:
Metadata of one Polish act by ELI id (e.g. "DU/1964/59"): status, whether it is in force,
dates, keywords, and related acts (amending acts, consolidated texts "Inf. o tekście
jednolitym", Constitutional Tribunal rulings, ...).
tools.name: legal_eli_act

tools.description:
Text of a Polish act by ELI id; with `article` ("133", "133a", "133^1") only that article.

wording="current" (default): the newest consolidated text ("tekst jednolity") of the act,
HTML or else its PDF. Amendments published after that consolidation are NOT in it; they are
listed in amended_after_consolidation ({eli, promulgation, date_unknown}) -- tell the reader to
check them. consolidation_date_inferred=true means the cut-off was not published and a
conservative earlier date was used, so the list may over-report. Without any
consolidation the act's own text is used and every amending act is listed.
wording="original": the act's HTML text as originally published.
tools.name: legal_eli_act_text

tools.description:

title: words of the act title (e.g. "kodeks rodzinny"); keyword: ELI subject keyword;
type: act type such as "Ustawa", "Rozporządzenie", "Obwieszczenie". Returns ELI ids
(e.g. "DU/1964/59") to pass to legal_eli_act / legal_eli_act_text.
tools.name: legal_eli_search

tools.description:
Search scientific literature (PubMed, Europe PMC, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, arXiv, ...)
in one federated query. Each item has a stable `id` for research_literature_record, upstream
ids (doi, pmid), a canonical `url` and the abstract. Default sources: all the engine has
enabled; `sources_failed` lists any that errored or are not available. Can take ~10-60 s.
Abstracts are capped (default 1500 chars) to keep the result small; quote from
research_literature_record, which returns the full abstract.
tools.name: research_literature_search
